source: T.C. Aile ve Sosyal Hizmetler Bakanlığı — Erişilebilirlik Kılavuzu — Binalar (2nd ed., 2024, ISBN 978-625-8402-08-7)
notes: Each top-level key matches an ObstacleCategory enum value used in the backend (apps/reports/models.py) and frontend (types/report.ts).
The 'code' field is what gets persisted on a report.
The 'label' is the short user-facing chip text — already phrased qualitatively so the user does not need to measure.
'short' is one sentence the form may show under the chip as a hint.
'requirement' quotes the underlying standard (with the actual measurement from the PDF) for the detail screen.
'why' explains in plain language who is affected and why it matters.
'pdfRef' cites the section in the source PDF.
OTHER category and any category not listed here intentionally has no violation chips.

BROKEN_RAMP.label: Too steep
BROKEN_RAMP.short: The slope feels too steep to climb safely.
BROKEN_RAMP.requirement: Maximum slope is 8% (1:12) for rises up to 15 cm. For taller rises the limit is lower: 7% up to 50 cm, 6% up to 100 cm, 5% above 100 cm.
BROKEN_RAMP.why: A steep ramp is unsafe for a wheelchair user without assistance and dangerous to descend in either direction.

BROKEN_RAMP.label: Too narrow
BROKEN_RAMP.short: Not wide enough for a wheelchair to pass.
BROKEN_RAMP.requirement: Clear width must be at least 100 cm, measured between handrails or curbs.
BROKEN_RAMP.why: A wheelchair plus handrails will not physically fit in a narrower ramp.

BROKEN_RAMP.label: No handrails
BROKEN_RAMP.short: Handrails are missing on one or both sides.
BROKEN_RAMP.requirement: Handrails required on both sides at 90 cm and 70 cm height for any rise greater than 15 cm or length greater than 2 m.
BROKEN_RAMP.why: People with limited balance, ambulatory disabled users and elderly users rely on handrails to use a ramp safely.

BROKEN_RAMP.label: Slippery or damaged surface
BROKEN_RAMP.short: Surface is wet, smooth, cracked, or unstable.
BROKEN_RAMP.requirement: Surface must be flat, stable and non-slip in both wet and dry conditions (TS 13882 — outdoor ramps at least R11).
BROKEN_RAMP.why: Slippery or uneven ramps cause falls, especially when wet.

BROKEN_RAMP.label: No landing at top or bottom
BROKEN_RAMP.short: No flat resting space at the ends.
BROKEN_RAMP.requirement: Flat landing of at least 150 × 150 cm at the top, bottom, every change of direction, and every 9 m along the ramp.
BROKEN_RAMP.why: Wheelchair users need a flat space to rest, open a door, or turn around.

BROKEN_RAMP.label: No edge protection
BROKEN_RAMP.short: Open edge with nothing to keep wheels from slipping off.
BROKEN_RAMP.requirement: Protective curb of at least 5 cm on any open edge of the ramp and its landings.
BROKEN_RAMP.why: Keeps a wheelchair wheel or cane from slipping off the side of the ramp.

NARROW_SIDEWALK.label: Too narrow to pass
NARROW_SIDEWALK.short: Not wide enough for a wheelchair or stroller.
NARROW_SIDEWALK.requirement: Minimum clear walking path of 100 cm; 150 cm recommended where two-way traffic is expected.
NARROW_SIDEWALK.why: A wheelchair, walker, or stroller cannot pass through a narrower path.

NARROW_SIDEWALK.label: Obstacle in path
NARROW_SIDEWALK.short: Pole, sign, bench or planter sticking into the walking area.
NARROW_SIDEWALK.requirement: Nothing should protrude more than 10 cm into the walking path between 68.5 cm and 220 cm height; clear headroom is 220 cm.
NARROW_SIDEWALK.why: Protruding objects are invisible to blind users using a cane below knee level and cause head and shoulder injuries.

NARROW_SIDEWALK.label: No curb ramp at crossing
NARROW_SIDEWALK.short: Sidewalk meets the road with a step.
NARROW_SIDEWALK.requirement: A curb ramp is required wherever a sidewalk meets a road; a tactile warning surface should mark the top.
NARROW_SIDEWALK.why: Without a curb ramp wheelchair users cannot cross the street at all.

NARROW_SIDEWALK.label: Uneven surface
NARROW_SIDEWALK.short: Surface is bumpy, sloped sideways, or has small steps.
NARROW_SIDEWALK.requirement: Surface must be flat and stable; any level difference greater than 1.3 cm must be bridged by a ramp.
NARROW_SIDEWALK.why: Small steps trip elderly users and tip wheelchairs sideways.

DAMAGED_SURFACE.label: Cracks or holes
DAMAGED_SURFACE.short: Visible cracks, potholes or missing pieces of pavement.
DAMAGED_SURFACE.requirement: Walking surfaces must be continuous, flat and stable.
DAMAGED_SURFACE.why: Cracks catch cane tips, wheelchair wheels and stroller wheels and cause falls.

DAMAGED_SURFACE.label: Loose tiles or stones
DAMAGED_SURFACE.short: Paving stones move or wobble when stepped on.
DAMAGED_SURFACE.requirement: Surface materials must be firmly fixed and stable.
DAMAGED_SURFACE.why: Loose paving shifts under weight and causes falls.

DAMAGED_SURFACE.label: Grid or drain gaps too wide
DAMAGED_SURFACE.short: Drain or grid slots run along the walking direction or are wide.
DAMAGED_SURFACE.requirement: Drain and grid openings must be at most 13 mm wide, oriented perpendicular to the walking direction.
DAMAGED_SURFACE.why: Wider or parallel gaps trap canes, wheelchair wheels and stroller wheels.

DAMAGED_SURFACE.label: Step or sudden drop
DAMAGED_SURFACE.short: There is a step where a ramp should be.
DAMAGED_SURFACE.requirement: Any level difference greater than 1.3 cm must be bridged by a ramp.
DAMAGED_SURFACE.why: Even a small step is an impassable barrier for a wheelchair.

DAMAGED_SURFACE.label: Slippery when wet
DAMAGED_SURFACE.requirement: Surface must remain non-slip in wet conditions (TS 13882; outdoor walking surfaces at least R10).
DAMAGED_SURFACE.why: Most accessibility falls happen on wet, smooth surfaces.

ROAD_CONSTRUCTION.label: No accessible detour
ROAD_CONSTRUCTION.short: The path is blocked and there is no marked alternative.
ROAD_CONSTRUCTION.requirement: Construction that closes a pedestrian path must provide an accessible alternative route.
ROAD_CONSTRUCTION.why: Without a detour the area becomes impassable for wheelchair users.

ROAD_CONSTRUCTION.label: Detour not marked
ROAD_CONSTRUCTION.short: It is unclear where pedestrians should walk.
ROAD_CONSTRUCTION.requirement: Temporary routes must be clearly marked with both visual and tactile signs.
ROAD_CONSTRUCTION.why: Blind and low-vision users cannot perceive an unmarked detour.

ROAD_CONSTRUCTION.label: Open hazard, no barrier
ROAD_CONSTRUCTION.short: Open trenches, machinery or holes with nothing protecting pedestrians.
ROAD_CONSTRUCTION.requirement: Open excavations, scaffolding bases and equipment must be enclosed by solid barriers detectable by a cane.
ROAD_CONSTRUCTION.why: Open hazards in walking paths cause serious injury, especially to blind users.

ROAD_CONSTRUCTION.label: Temporary surface unsafe
ROAD_CONSTRUCTION.short: Metal plates, boards or planks are loose or have gaps.
ROAD_CONSTRUCTION.requirement: Temporary walking surfaces must be flat, stable, non-slip and gap-free.
ROAD_CONSTRUCTION.why: Rocking metal plates and loose boards tip wheelchairs and catch canes.

BLOCKED_PATH.label: Permanently blocked
BLOCKED_PATH.short: The path is closed off and shows no sign of being temporary.
BLOCKED_PATH.requirement: Pedestrian paths must remain unobstructed (at least 100 cm clear).
BLOCKED_PATH.why: A permanent block forces a long, often unsafe detour into the road.

BLOCKED_PATH.label: Vehicle blocking path
BLOCKED_PATH.short: A parked car, scooter or delivery vehicle is in the walking area.
BLOCKED_PATH.requirement: Vehicles must not be parked on pedestrian routes.
BLOCKED_PATH.why: Forces wheelchair users into the road.

BLOCKED_PATH.label: Overgrown vegetation
BLOCKED_PATH.short: Branches or bushes have grown into the walking area.
BLOCKED_PATH.requirement: Vegetation must not encroach on the 100 cm walking corridor or 220 cm head clearance.
BLOCKED_PATH.why: Branches at head height are dangerous to blind users who cannot detect them with a cane.

BLOCKED_PATH.label: Trash or debris
BLOCKED_PATH.short: Garbage bags, leaves, or building debris pile up in the path.
BLOCKED_PATH.requirement: Walking surfaces must be kept clear.
BLOCKED_PATH.why: Tripping hazard, especially for low-vision and elderly users.

BROKEN_ELEVATOR.label: Out of order
BROKEN_ELEVATOR.requirement: A functioning elevator is required for accessible vertical circulation in multi-floor buildings.
BROKEN_ELEVATOR.why: When the only elevator is out of order, every floor above ground level is inaccessible.

BROKEN_ELEVATOR.label: Cabin too small
BROKEN_ELEVATOR.short: A wheelchair does not fit inside.
BROKEN_ELEVATOR.requirement: Cabin must be at least 120 × 150 cm (1.80 m²).
BROKEN_ELEVATOR.why: A standard wheelchair will not fit inside smaller cabins.

BROKEN_ELEVATOR.label: Door too narrow
BROKEN_ELEVATOR.short: A wheelchair does not fit through the door.
BROKEN_ELEVATOR.requirement: Clear door opening at least 90 cm wide.
BROKEN_ELEVATOR.why: Narrower doors cannot admit a standard wheelchair.

BROKEN_ELEVATOR.label: No audio announcement
BROKEN_ELEVATOR.short: Floors are not announced out loud.
BROKEN_ELEVATOR.requirement: Audible announcement of the arriving floor is required inside the cabin.
BROKEN_ELEVATOR.why: Blind users have no way to know which floor they are on.

BROKEN_ELEVATOR.label: No Braille / tactile buttons
BROKEN_ELEVATOR.short: Buttons are touchscreen or flat with no raised markings.
BROKEN_ELEVATOR.requirement: Buttons must be tactile with Braille labels, contrasting in color with their background.
BROKEN_ELEVATOR.why: Blind users cannot operate a flat touchscreen.

BROKEN_ELEVATOR.label: Door closes too fast
BROKEN_ELEVATOR.short: Not enough time to enter or exit.
BROKEN_ELEVATOR.requirement: The door must remain open for at least 6 seconds.
BROKEN_ELEVATOR.why: Wheelchair users and people with mobility aids cannot board in time.

BROKEN_ELEVATOR.label: Step or gap at door
BROKEN_ELEVATOR.short: Cabin floor does not line up with the building floor.
BROKEN_ELEVATOR.requirement: Cabin floor must align with the landing within ±1 cm; no threshold.
BROKEN_ELEVATOR.why: Any step or gap can trap a wheelchair wheel or trip a user.

INACCESSIBLE_RESTROOM.label: Door too narrow
INACCESSIBLE_RESTROOM.short: A wheelchair does not fit through the door.
INACCESSIBLE_RESTROOM.requirement: Clear door opening at least 90 cm; door should open outward.
INACCESSIBLE_RESTROOM.why: Wheelchairs cannot fit through a narrower door.

INACCESSIBLE_RESTROOM.label: No turning space inside
INACCESSIBLE_RESTROOM.short: There is no room to turn a wheelchair around.
INACCESSIBLE_RESTROOM.requirement: A clear maneuvering circle of 150 cm diameter is required inside the accessible WC.
INACCESSIBLE_RESTROOM.why: Without it, a wheelchair user cannot turn around to leave.

INACCESSIBLE_RESTROOM.label: No grab bars
INACCESSIBLE_RESTROOM.short: Toilet has no support bars beside it.
INACCESSIBLE_RESTROOM.requirement: Grab bars on at least one side (preferably both), positioned 25–35 cm above seat height.
INACCESSIBLE_RESTROOM.why: Transferring from a wheelchair to a toilet requires grab bars for safety.

INACCESSIBLE_RESTROOM.label: Door opens inward
INACCESSIBLE_RESTROOM.short: Door swings into the stall and blocks access.
INACCESSIBLE_RESTROOM.requirement: Accessible WC doors must open outward or slide.
INACCESSIBLE_RESTROOM.why: If a user falls inside, an inward-opening door cannot be opened from outside to help them.

INACCESSIBLE_RESTROOM.label: No emergency call button
INACCESSIBLE_RESTROOM.short: There is no way to call for help.
INACCESSIBLE_RESTROOM.requirement: Emergency call cord reachable both while standing (around 122 cm) and from the floor (30–50 cm).
INACCESSIBLE_RESTROOM.why: A user who has fallen must be able to call for help from the floor.

NARROW_CORRIDOR.label: Too narrow
NARROW_CORRIDOR.requirement: Clear corridor width must be at least 120 cm.
NARROW_CORRIDOR.why: Narrower corridors cannot accommodate a wheelchair, especially with another person passing.

NARROW_CORRIDOR.label: Cannot turn corner
NARROW_CORRIDOR.short: Wheelchair gets stuck at the turn.
NARROW_CORRIDOR.requirement: At 90° turns, clear width must be at least 120 cm in both directions; 150 cm recommended.
NARROW_CORRIDOR.why: A wheelchair cannot pivot in a tighter corner.

NARROW_CORRIDOR.label: Obstacles in corridor
NARROW_CORRIDOR.short: Cabinets, signs or fixtures stick into the corridor.
NARROW_CORRIDOR.requirement: No object may protrude more than 10 cm into the corridor between 68.5 cm and 220 cm height.
NARROW_CORRIDOR.why: Protruding objects at chest or head height are undetectable by a cane.

NARROW_CORRIDOR.label: Low headroom
NARROW_CORRIDOR.short: Ceiling, ducts or stair undersides hang low.
NARROW_CORRIDOR.requirement: Minimum clear height of 220 cm along the entire corridor.
NARROW_CORRIDOR.why: Low ceilings cause head injuries, especially for blind users.

HEAVY_DOOR.label: Too heavy to push
HEAVY_DOOR.short: Door takes significant effort to open.
HEAVY_DOOR.requirement: Doors must open without excessive force; closers should slow the door near the end.
HEAVY_DOOR.why: Heavy doors are unusable from a wheelchair or with limited grip strength.

HEAVY_DOOR.label: Threshold or step at door
HEAVY_DOOR.short: There is a bump or step in the doorway.
HEAVY_DOOR.requirement: No threshold is preferred; if unavoidable, max 1.3 cm and chamfered.
HEAVY_DOOR.why: Even a small threshold can stop a wheelchair or trip a user.

HEAVY_DOOR.label: Knob handle (not a lever)
HEAVY_DOOR.short: Door has a round knob that must be twisted.
HEAVY_DOOR.requirement: Lever or D-shaped pull handles only — no round knobs.
HEAVY_DOOR.why: Knobs cannot be operated by people with limited hand strength or no grip.

HEAVY_DOOR.label: Handle too high or low
HEAVY_DOOR.short: Handle is out of comfortable reach.
HEAVY_DOOR.requirement: Handle height between 90 cm and 110 cm above the floor.
HEAVY_DOOR.why: Handles outside this range are out of reach from a wheelchair or for children.

HEAVY_DOOR.label: Doorway too narrow
HEAVY_DOOR.short: A wheelchair does not fit through.
HEAVY_DOOR.requirement: Interior doors must have a clear opening of at least 90 cm when open.
HEAVY_DOOR.why: Standard wheelchairs need at least 90 cm to pass through.

SLIPPERY_FLOOR.label: Wet floor, no warning sign
SLIPPERY_FLOOR.short: Floor is wet but nothing alerts you.
SLIPPERY_FLOOR.requirement: Wet surfaces must be marked with visible warning signs.
SLIPPERY_FLOOR.why: Unmarked wet floors cause falls, especially for elderly users.

SLIPPERY_FLOOR.label: Polished or glossy
SLIPPERY_FLOOR.short: Surface looks shiny and feels slick.
SLIPPERY_FLOOR.requirement: Floors must be non-slip per TS 13882 (R10 minimum for interior public areas).
SLIPPERY_FLOOR.why: Highly polished floors are dangerous for anyone with reduced balance.

SLIPPERY_FLOOR.label: No mat at entrance
SLIPPERY_FLOOR.short: Wet shoes track water onto the floor.
SLIPPERY_FLOOR.requirement: Entrance areas should have a non-slip mat in wet weather.
SLIPPERY_FLOOR.why: Wet shoes turn interior floors into slip hazards.

SLIPPERY_FLOOR.label: Recently mopped, no sign
SLIPPERY_FLOOR.short: Floor is wet from cleaning with nothing warning you.
SLIPPERY_FLOOR.requirement: Cleaning in progress requires visible wet-floor signs.
SLIPPERY_FLOOR.why: Most cleaning-related falls happen on freshly mopped floors with no warning.
